  - This paper introduces the System 0/1/2/3 framework as an extension of dual-process theory, employing a quad-process model of cognition. Expanding upon System 1 (fast, intuitive thinking) and System 2 (slow, deliberative thinking), we incorporate System 0, which represents pre-cognitive embodied processes, and System 3, which encompasses collective intelligence and symbol emergence. We contextualize this model within Bergson's philosophy by adopting multi-scale time theory to unify the diverse temporal dynamics of cognition. System 0 emphasizes morphological computation and passive dynamics, illustrating how physical embodiment enables adaptive behavior without explicit neural processing

Note above (media analysis: Chris Hedges et al), the use of proper names to anchor a Knowledge Graph heavy on personalities (which may include fictional characters, from cartoons to mythological pantheons). Concepts belong too e.g. Transcendentalism, Pragmatism, IVM, AI, open source, and so on (some of these are proper names, but not of people or personalities). Timeline information (chronology) is often relevant.  
  
The idea is as you start adding nodes and edges, starting the connections yourself, AI kicks in and starts growing the network, annotating edges with useful information about the nature of each relationship. The focus on personalities has to do with maxing bandwidth as interpersonal connections, even if only one way and asynchronous, tend to be information-rich in ways we readily understand (being humans ourselves).  
  
The edges we draw (such as I’ve implied if not literally drawn in my [Graph Theory slide deck](https://youtu.be/rEZyoxPbE9s)) likewise receive the benefit of additional annotation by AI (other users by proxy) by default, as the whole point of the app is to get help from AI in filling in gaps, even while fine tuning a sense of relevance, so as not to flood the scope with extranea. Sometimes the measure of “optimal” is not “the most” but “a few, of the highest quality”. Not that these approaches are mutually exclusive; we’ll get help with both strategies, and others scholarship contributes.

This display instrument below shows how 12 linear combinations of quadrays {2, 1, 1, 0} correspond to the corners of a cuboctahedron, meaning a neighboring tangent sphere relative to the central sphere. 

Given Basis Quadrays:  
  
A ← (1, 0, 0, 0)  
B ← (0, 1, 0, 0)  
C ←(0, 0, 1, 0)  
D ← (0, 0, 0, 1)  
  
multiply any one of them by 2, any two others by 1 (i.e. take as is), and don’t use the fourth one at all (multiply by 0), and add the results. Quadray vectors add the same way XYZ vectors do, tip-to-tail.  
  
The resultant vector will be from ORIGIN (0,0,0,0) to one of the 12 corners of the cuboctahedron, of radial and circumferential edges DIAMETER (the same length as the edges of the home base tetrahedron).

- **Omni-Medium Plummeting Device** **[https://coda.io/d/_d0SvdI3KSto/_suh-4GTC](https://coda.io/d/_d0SvdI3KSto/_suh-4GTC)** 

An important meme in our corpus is the omni-medium transport, a theoretical device we’re always pushing to a next level, even as milestone prototypes are possibly achieved.  
  
For example, the “flying car”, able to drive along highways, and take to the air, has made great strides and is now on the brink of mass industrial commercialization. But that leaves other media out of the equation: the water’s surface, and underwater. When will the floating bus become a sub?  
  
The same floating bus is also able to take wing or drive up on land. 



And even with all that, we could push further, taking her into outer space, perhaps to the Moon and back.  
  
What we appreciate is that, wholly independently of the practicality of such a vehicle, merely contemplating its possibility, as a futuristic device, feeds our ability to think scientifically as well as mythopoetically.  
  
The chariots of the gods and goddesses have always served as food for our relatively feeble imaginations. Our speculations regarding UAPs and what propels them, anti-gravity engines and so on, keeps our imaginations alive with possibilities and that in itself is a service we need, much as we need random number generators.  
  
Science fiction is a shared social good, a repository of our hopes, our dreams, our nightmares, our paranoias.  
  
Along these lines, I suggest a new Art category in this M4W Coda wherein we test out what we get around prompting for such an omni-medium transportation solution, as well as subsets thereof. It’s fine to focus on airplane-meets-car option, neglecting for the time being the mirroring water-underwater bus-sub option. 

Yellow Submarine meets Further.

### From AK 

I will write a few letters about my priorities going forward.  My goal is to foster a culture of investigation.  I am very glad that my own study group, Living by Truth, will start to meet this Wednesday.  We will use Daniel's zoom room. (Please let me know if you will join us and I will send you the link.)  We will meet for one hour starting at 7:00 am US Pacific Coast, 17:00 Eastern Europe.  
* First, Bill, Marcus, Daniel will talk about the questions they are investigating, how that is going.

* Then I will talk about my own investigation and explain how Wondrous Wisdom could be relevant for our investigations.

* Then we'll have discussion on how we can relate this all.  We'll keep in mind a couple of shared questions:  "How do languages work?" and also "How can we foster an investigatory culture?"  

Bill is investigating, What kind of universe do we live in?

[https://www.e-c-o.net/wiki/Econet/Universe](https://www.e-c-o.net/wiki/Econet/Universe)

Marcus explores, How can we develop a universal sign language for all people?

[https://www.e-c-o.net/wiki/Econet/UniversalSignLanguage](https://www.e-c-o.net/wiki/Econet/UniversalSignLanguage)

Daniel asks, What are the enabling conditions for symbolic coherence?  Daniel, does this relate to your recent video on "Generalized Notation Notation"  
[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y3-FMoaEZYE](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y3-FMoaEZYE)

GNN is described in this paper [https://zenodo.org/records/7803328](https://zenodo.org/records/7803328) and available for installation here  
[https://github.com/ActiveInferenceInstitute/GeneralizedNotationNotation](https://github.com/ActiveInferenceInstitute/GeneralizedNotationNotation) 

The point is to describe a generative model (by which the mind conceives its environment) in three forms as visual information, linguistic information, executable information.  

  


I think the GNN presents the information as preferred by each of the three minds - the unconscious answering mind prefers image, the conscious questioning mind prefers language, and the investigatory mind prefers explicit procedures.  You can see that i have included it in the Theory Translator if you go to this new page on "latest entries" (the ones I have curated)  
[https://www.theorytranslator.com/index.php?structure=latest](https://www.theorytranslator.com/index.php?structure=latest)  
I have also made a link to the "new suggestions" that you have contributed to the pipeline (thank you very much, Bill, Marcus, Daniel and all!)  
[https://www.theorytranslator.com/index.php?structure=new](https://www.theorytranslator.com/index.php?structure=new)

  


I myself am investigating triangle geometry, how to think of it as a language of actions, by which issues come to matter for the unconscious mind, and a language of concepts, by which meaning arises for the conscious mind.  
[https://www.math4wisdom.com/wiki/Research/TriangleCenters](https://www.math4wisdom.com/wiki/Research/TriangleCenters)

Given an arbitrary triangle, the ancient Greeks knew of four special points ("triangle centers") they could construct. In the 1800s and 1900s geometers came up with several hundred such triangle center constructions. Nowadays there is an Encyclopedia with 60,000.  I believe that implicit within all of these constructions is a language which generates the centers.  I want to sort out that language by which one can interact with an arbitrary triangle, so to say, speak its language.  Similarly, there are all manner of languages by which we can interact - ballet, chess, humor, music.  What is the language for interacting with the universe?  I believe that all of these languages are basically the same.  So i am studying triangle geometry because that is for me the simplest language I can think of for figuring out how this works.

  


Our effort to work together is most important.  I will write more about my other priorities as an investigator, and reaching out to others, and providing for myself.  I will conclude with some facts about my livelihood.

Under the heading of which tetrahedron volume formulae work with distance (i.e. edge lengths):  
  
Piero della Francesca (PdF) and Caley-Menger (CM) algorithms are clearly amenable to “S3 treatment” i.e. they already come with constants we only need modify by sqrt(9/8).  
  
In contrast, the Gerald de Jong algorithm has no clear derivation from a prior XYZ-based formula and yet outputs the same tetravolume answers as the other two.  
  
Gerald recalls deriving his solution analytically, on a train in the Netherlands, and then losing his notes and ability to rederive, so there’s a memory hole, not the first in the lore, that only adds to the mystery.  
  
It’s as if PdF and CM are bridging algorithms, coming from XYZ originally, but in [GdJ’s formula](https://flic.kr/p/231UJ5S) we kick away the ladder and compute volume natively in our IVM “tetraverse”. Tom Ace’s quadrays-based formula has a similar flavor.

A standard intro to Python vid takes the O’Reilly Head First [tm] approach of: “meta cog about cognition first” i.e. how do we best learn (pedagogy, andragogy)? We talk about how “wrong images” (yet per Wittgenstein bewitching, tempting, hard to shake loose) might get in our way.  
  
Take the concept of *variables* for instance, so often dwelt upon as “boxes with names, with values inside”. But in Python if x names a list, and then we say “y equal sign  (assignment operator) x”, then y is a name for the same object in memory (no copy made), like another luggage tag on a suitcase, like another string to the same balloon, those are the better metaphors.

    - Many Luggage tag model





    - Many strings to same balloon model:



    - Many remotes to same TV model:

  
This is one of my favorite teaching mnemonics in that a TV remote’s buttons come pre-wired to the “special names” built in to the Python language (dunder this, dunder that), wherefore objects come pre-equipped with the ability to “understand” (receive signals from) button pushes, referring to the  lightweight syntax (dot notation, calling methods, accessing attributes) animating (operating) the possibly memory-heavy objects on the heap, in memory.

    - It’s not like “variables are like boxes” is a wrong analogy across the board, as if computer science got it wrong and Python is now somehow revealing the real deal, it’s more that each computer language comes with its own “most fitting” mental imagery and to “carry over” the same “mindset” from one language to another is similar to the shortcoming of overfitting. Python was aiming to economize on memory and not have simple assignment operations result in what could be massive duplications in memory; better to have a syntax that makes you work for it, if you really want another copy of some object.

    - Every language intro might start with a “back to basics” meta cog moment wherein we revector some preconceptions we have reason to imagine might be lurking in the average reader’s priors. Better to address those inhibiting factors directly than let them linger, assuming the reader (student) is amenable to adopting new heuristics for the purposes of mastering the new language in question. Natural language learnings are used to making these “concessions” (freeing up of one’s consciousness by revisiting one’s choices at a more fundamental level, because between languages).

## **Description**

This paper enacts a computational juxtaposition between William Blake's 1790 illuminated poem "The Marriage of Heaven and Hell", and a personal-poetic perspective on ecological psychology. This paper is rendered as a dual-column PDF reflecting Blake's insight — "Without contraries is no progression" — in its very architecture. The left column ("Synthesis of Agent and Niche") transposes Blake's prophetic vision into the mathematical language of free energy principle, active inference, biosemiotics, and niche construction, revealing how poetic intuitions about Energy versus Reason, body versus soul, and heaven versus hell prefigure modern understandings of embodied cognition, self-organizing systems, and the thermodynamic imperatives driving bio-cultural evolution. The right column preserves Blake's original text, creating a stereoscopic, or duck-rabbit, minimum-2 effect where the 18th- and 21st-century perspectives textographically illuminate each other, rendering the other newly legible through their juxtaposition. Taken rhetorically, the work argues that Blake's romantic vision and contemporary cognitive science constitute complementary expressions of concepts like: universe, life, general and specific situationality, generativity, intra-action, the necessity of opposition and provocation, and the orientation of energetic engagement over passive observation.

The project's epistemic stance ("Definitely Speculative & Claude 4.5-pilled") acknowledges its experimental nature while insisting that etching (on) the edge often requires crossing boundaries. The medium of composition — Python scripts that transform Markdown files into a PDF, with calibrated typography and dual-gradient backgrounds distinguishing the columns separated and connected by a dashed line — demonstrates how modern computational infrastructure can serve as amplification of humanistic inquiry. Only and actually: execution and rendering of this hybrid text performs the synthesis it describes (or at least one like it!). From that morpho-semiosis, there is a suggestion that the marriage of poetic and scientific, visionary and formal, yields insights unavailable to either, as taken or given alone. In that way the work operates as awareness literature, synthetic milestone, technical writing draft, pragmatic cognitive fiction, and open source computational artifact published to Github and Zenodo in September 2025.

  - **Triangular Network Model for the Neural Basis of Calligraphy**  
[Nai Ding](https://nyaspubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/authored-by/Ding/Nai)  
[https://nyaspubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/nyas.70153](https://nyaspubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/nyas.70153)  
Calligraphy is the artistic expression of written language, similar to how songs artistically express verbal language. This article proposes a triangular-network model for neural processing of calligraphy, which builds on recent findings about the neurophysiology of writing and theories about neural processing of other art forms. This model emphasizes that calligraphy appreciation relies on both visual spatial features and temporal motoric features of the actual or mentally simulated writing process. While the appreciation of visual spatial features may engage neural mechanisms encoding other visual arts, the appreciation of temporal motoric features may engage a prediction-based mechanism—the brain actively predicts the writing movement, and the fulfillment or violation of these predictions generates pleasure, similar to how predictions may contribute to music appreciation. Furthermore, it is hypothesized that practicing calligraphy enriches the motoric representation of writing by directing attention to otherwise subconscious movement units, similar to how dancing is mindful movement. The triangular-network model provides a theoretical framework for neural encoding of calligraphy, generates testable predictions, and forges a link to neural encoding of other art forms.

  - The Martian Math moniker is multi-layered. In the full blown science fiction tale I tell, Earthling kids are being trained in ET math, but the ETs are here, not on Mars, and they want to learn from us about hydroelectric dams, whereas Earthlings have a lot to learn from them, so a 2-way street is posited. Let’s build a dam together; a jumping off point into electromagnetics topics.

  - Synergetics is more coming from the ETs than from the Earthlings; ergo Synergetics seems alien, strange, weird (pedagogical positives when managed properly). The Earthling kids in our Martian Math class also learn how the ET kids learn Earthling math. TetraBook goes here. Tested at Reed College and other places around town c/o Saturday Academy.

  - And once we’re in the mood (mode) for science fiction: War of the Worlds and the Orson Welles reading thereof are important, is a fork to both H.G. Wells and his non-fiction (world between wars) as well as fiction (Time Machine), and to Orson Welles going forward into Film Studies (Media Studies). That War of the Worlds anticipates the virus (as yet unknown) in some dimensions (see web pages) is a jumping off point into biology, virology, crystallography, STEM in general.

  - Finally, Martian Math may be contextualized in its Silicon Forest context as one of four maths: Casino, Supermarket, Martian, Neolithic. The idea here is Martian is forward facing futuristic (all the future), Neolithic faces back in the direction of prehistory (all the past), Casino covers risk and chance, probability and Supermarket is all about logistics commerce and distribution. Martian - Neolithic is a time arc, whereas every age, every time slice (every now), has to compute in terms of possibilities, probabilities, and operate logistically using inventory (the BE DO HAVE of GST).

  - However it’s all supposed to stay flexible and optional. There’s no one right way, but when I do it I experiment and expand in specific directions, as would anyone.

  - DemoCreate: declarative, deterministic audio-visual demo generation for software packages and research papers.  
Paper: [https://zenodo.org/records/20693217](https://zenodo.org/records/20693217)  
Code: [https://github.com/docxology/democreate](https://github.com/docxology/democreate)  
Video: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GbsZXNjqHuM](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GbsZXNjqHuM)  
DemoCreate generates audio-visual demos of software — codebase tours, website walkthroughs, and terminal/CLI demos — from a single declarative, deterministic spine. A Demo is an ordered action stream plus narration chunks, merging CodeVideo's event-sourced virtual-IDE model with VSpeak's chunk/trigger model. Every heavy backend (TTS via Kokoro/Chatterbox, transcription via Whisper, capture via mss/Playwright, animation via Manim, assembly via MoviePy/ffmpeg) sits behind an abstract interface with a pure-Python deterministic default, so the package produces a real demo with only light dependencies and upgrades when extras are installed. On-screen actions are anchored to spoken trigger words via TTS→STT synchronization: narration audio is generated, transcribed back to word-level timestamps, and used to align the action stream with the narration.

Code: [https://github.com/ActiveInferenceInstitute/COGANT](https://github.com/ActiveInferenceInstitute/COGANT)  
COGANT (Codebase-to-GNN Translation) deterministically converts software repositories into structured Active Inference artifacts expressed in the Active Inference Institute's Generalized Notation Notation (GNN). It is an evidence compiler: it propagates reviewable program facts through a finite fixpoint rule pipeline and emits graph, matrix, provenance, visualization, and round-trip artifacts with confidence and provenance, rather than a single opaque embedding. A reverse synthesizer reconstructs a runnable Python package from an emitted GNN bundle, closing a forward-reverse-forward evaluation loop. This is the first public release (v0.6.0).
